command-dispatcher-prep.title: Meet Surveyor Delta
body: Mission IRIS above the Mawrth Vallis plateau enters a major new phase. Joining light scout drone Sigma is the fleet's second specialized vehicle — heavy survey drone KARTOGRĀFS 'Delta'.

Delta is equipped with reinforced carbon armor, high-torque dual-rotor lifting shrouds, and a full suite of precision exploration hardware: a topography LiDAR scanner, multispectral cameras, and mineral spectrometers. To direct these scientific instruments, base IRIS transmits discrete single-character dispatch codes (`'S'`, `'L'`, `'C'`, `'H'`).

Evaluating such commands with a lengthy `if / else if` cascade quickly becomes cluttered: the expression `cmd ==` must be repeated on every single branch. C++ provides a specialized construct named `switch` — a fast and elegant command dispatcher designed to route execution based on discrete integer or character codes.

more.title: Why switch compiles to jump tables in machine code
body: In an `if / else if` chain, the CPU must evaluate each condition sequentially. If a cascade contains 10 branches, reaching the final branch requires 10 distinct comparison operations — linear time complexity O(N).

In contrast, for a dense `switch` statement, modern C++ compilers frequently synthesize a jump table. This is an array-like table of machine code addresses stored directly in memory: the numeric value of the selector character or integer acts as an immediate index offset, allowing the CPU to execute a single branch instruction straight to the matching target.

Jump tables provide constant execution time O(1) regardless of branch count. In mission-critical avionics firmware where control loops operate at strict millisecond deadlines, `switch` delivers deterministic, low-latency command routing.
Sources: Bjarne Stroustrup, 'The C++ Programming Language' (4th Edition, Addison-Wesley); Agner Fog, 'Optimizing subroutines in assembly language'.

switch-syntax-and-case.title: The switch statement and case labels
body: The `switch` statement evaluates a single selector variable and branches directly to the matching `case` label.

> Strict type constraint rule:
> The `switch` statement accepts ONLY integral types (`int`, `short`) and characters (`char`). In C++, it is strictly forbidden to use `switch` with floating-point numbers (`double`) or strings (`string`)!
Every `case` branch typically concludes with a `break;` statement. This signals to the compiler that the required actions are complete and execution should jump out of the `switch` block.
compareCaptions: Clean switch dispatcher: variable named once, discrete targets organized in a tidy column
Cluttered if/else cascade: repetitive syntax and redundant typing of variable cmd at every step

fallthrough-and-break.title: The break statement and fall-through
body: Unlike many other programming languages, C++ case labels do not implicitly terminate execution.

If you omit the `break;` statement at the conclusion of a case, execution does not halt: it simply 'falls through' into the subsequent `case` and executes its instructions as well! This behavior is known as fall-through.

!> **The missing break trap.** If you forget `break;`, the drone will execute the requested directive and continue cascading straight through all following cases until it hits a break or reaches the closing brace. In flight operations, this can accidentally trigger emergency subroutines!
fallthrough-and-break.alt: Diagram illustrating switch control flow: direct jump to matching case, execution, clean exit via break, and unintended fall-through when break is missing.

predict-switch-fallthrough.title: Predict fall-through behavior
predict-switch-fallthrough.task: What text will this program output? This is a prediction before running — trace the execution path carefully.
predict-switch-fallthrough.hint: Variable mode is 'B'. Find case 'B': and trace downward. Where does the next break; appear?
predict-switch-fallthrough.explain: Because `mode` equals `'B'`, execution jumps directly to `case 'B':` and prints `2`. Since no `break;` terminates this case, execution falls through into `case 'C':`, prints `3`, and only then encounters `break;`. The combined output is `23`.

surveyor-command-dispatcher.title: Surveyor Delta command dispatcher
surveyor-command-dispatcher.task:
Program drone Delta's instrument activator with `switch (command)`:
1. If `command == 'S'`, print `SURVEY: ACTIVE` and exit with `break;`.
2. If `command == 'L'`, print `LIDAR: ACTIVE` and exit with `break;`.
3. In all other cases (`default:`), print `COMMAND: UNKNOWN` and `break;`.
surveyor-command-dispatcher.hint: Use `switch (command) { case 'S': cout << "SURVEY: ACTIVE" << endl; break; ... }`.
surveyor-command-dispatcher.solutionNote: Because command holds 'S', the first case matches and prints SURVEY: ACTIVE.

find-switch-bug.title: Locate the missing break bug
find-switch-bug.task: Click on the line where a missing break causes execution to inadvertently fall through into emergency mode.
find-switch-bug.hint: Check what is missing at the conclusion of case 1: before the next case begins.
find-switch-bug.explain: The bug relates to case 1 branch (lines 8–9): after line 9 (`cout << "MODE: NORMAL" << endl;`), the `break;` statement is missing. Due to this omission, code 1 would execute normal mode and then immediately fall through into emergency mode from `case 2:`!

grouping-switch-cases.title: Stacking multiple case labels
body: Fall-through is not always a mistake. In fact, it provides a clean, idiomatic technique for binding multiple inputs to the exact same routine.
A classic aerospace telemetry example involves handling both uppercase and lowercase command characters. If an operator enters either `'M'` or `'m'`, both should initiate mapping mode:

+ **Label stacking.** Place `case 'M':` directly above `case 'm':` with no intervening statements and no `break`. If the first matches, execution falls directly into the shared body.
+ **Eliminating duplication.** This eliminates the need to copy-paste identical function calls and keeps the codebase concise and maintainable.
compareCaptions: Clean stacking: both case labels share a single implementation body and one break
Redundant duplication: copy-pasting the same instructions and break across multiple cases

dispatch-telemetry-mode.title: Interactive flight mode dispatcher
dispatch-telemetry-mode.task:
Program Surveyor Delta's mission mode selector using console `cin` (test input: `M`):
1. Read character `cmd` from `cin`.
2. Using `switch (cmd)` route execution: `'R'` -> `MODE: RECON`, `'M'` -> `MODE: MAPPING`, `'H'` -> `MODE: RETURN HOME`, and default (`default:`) -> `MODE: INVALID`.
3. Ensure every branch ends with `break;`.
dispatch-telemetry-mode.hint: Read with `cin >> cmd;`, then write `switch (cmd) { case 'R': ... break; ... }`.
dispatch-telemetry-mode.solutionNote: Given input 'M', the case 'M': branch executes and prints MODE: MAPPING.

ternary-operator.title: The ternary operator (?:)
body: Occasionally, flight code does not require an entire branching block with statements — it simply needs to select between two values based on a boolean condition.

syntax: {condition} ? {value_true} : {value_false}
- condition: boolean test yielding true or false
- ?: question mark separating condition from the truth value
- value_true: result returned if condition is true
- :: colon separating true result from false result
- value_false: result returned if condition is false

> Statement versus expression:
> The `if / else` construct is a **statement** — it directs control flow but does not evaluate to a value. The ternary operator `?:` is an **expression** — it computes and yields a concrete value that can be assigned directly to a variable or streamed into `cout`!

more.title: The ternary operator as an expression in C++
body: Because the ternary operator yields an expression value, it allows developers to initialize immutable `const` variables: `const int limit = is_eco ? 50 : 100;`. With an `if / else` statement, this would be impossible without declaring a non-const variable and reassigning it later.

Ternary expressions can also be embedded directly in output streams: `cout << (battery >= 20 ? "OK" : "LOW");`. Notice that parentheses around the ternary expression are mandatory here because stream insertion `<<` has higher operator precedence than `?:`.

Engineering rule of thumb: reserve the ternary operator strictly for simple, binary value assignments. Never nest ternary operators inside each other — nested conditionals drastically impair readability and introduce subtle logic bugs.

compareCaptions: Concise single line: ternary operator initializes variable directly with the chosen value
Verbose 5 lines: traditional if/else requires separate declaration and split assignment blocks

predict-ternary-output.title: Predict ternary evaluation
predict-ternary-output.task: What word will this program output?
predict-ternary-output.hint: Evaluate the condition battery >= 20 with battery equal to 15. Which value — before or after the colon — is selected?
predict-ternary-output.explain: Because `battery` holds 15, the condition `15 >= 20` evaluates to false. The ternary operator selects the expression following the colon `:`, so the program outputs `RED`.

delta-mission-controller.title: Bonus challenge: Surveyor instrument controller
delta-mission-controller.task:
Combine the ternary operator and `switch` inside Delta's instrument monitor (test input: `L 60`):
1. Read tool selector `char tool` and battery charge `int battery` from `cin`.
2. Use the ternary operator to choose power mode: if `battery >= 40`, power is `"FULL"`, otherwise `"ECO"`.
3. Handle `'L'`: print `TOOL: LIDAR | POWER: ` followed by power mode and newline.
4. Handle `'C'`: print `TOOL: CAMERA | POWER: ` followed by power mode and newline.
5. In all other cases (`default:`): print `TOOL: STANDBY` and newline.
delta-mission-controller.hint: Use `string power = (battery >= 40) ? "FULL" : "ECO";`, followed by `switch (tool)` with corresponding output lines.
delta-mission-controller.solutionNote: With input 'L' and 60, battery 60 >= 40 sets power mode to FULL, and case 'L': prints TOOL: LIDAR | POWER: FULL.

recap.title: Mission 11 summary: Command dispatcher active
body: Base IRIS confirms operational readiness: KARTOGRĀFS 'Delta' has joined the IRIS exploration squadron and processes incoming payload commands with high-speed dispatch logic.

| Construct | Syntax | Best aerospace application |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `if / else if` | `if (x < 10) ...` | Continuous ranges, floating-point numbers, multi-criteria expressions |
| `switch / case` | `switch (cmd) ...` | Discrete constants (char, int), rapid command dispatchers |
| Ternary `?:` | `cond ? a : b` | Compact inline value selection in assignments or direct streaming |

Next, in Chapter 12, awaits Block 2's major PRACTICUM: «Safety system». We will synthesize every branching and logical concept learned so far (`if`, `else`, `&&`, `||`, `!`, `switch`, `?:`) into a unified, resilient flight safety controller protecting both drones Sigma and Delta.
